events.comment: One-frame flags are cleared here; scene events read them in the next frame
Death has the highest priority
Timers

Sight: the player is seen when the line is clear (CanAttack) and within AggroRange. Aggro starts when the player is seen and ends MemoryTime seconds after the last sighting (then the enemy shakes its head and goes back to patrol)
Evolution timer: runs from first aggro, even if the player runs away
Last second before evolving: stop and telegraph (Dance for Blob)
Evolution dance: the Dance animation plays DanceRepeats times (it is short), then the enemy is ready to be replaced
Hit reaction: not during an attack or evolution, throttled, ignored with super armor
Looking into a dead-end (patrol) or giving up a chase: stand still, shake the head (No), then back to patrol
Attack
Movement: straight towards the target (flow-field can replace SetTarget later). Chasing is fast; patrolling (no aggro) walks slowly to the patrol waypoint
State -> animation (names are the original model animations)

Death: play the animation, destroy when it ends. CurrentAnim must already be Death (it is applied below, one frame later) or the previous animation would be checked. DeathTimeout is a safety net for a Death animation that loops.
The finished Death animation holds its last pose, so a corpse needs no more work
Dying and dead flying enemies fall to the ground instead of floating where they were killed
Apply the animation only when it changes
